Are you looking for information about the Franklin County Circuit Court? This guide will provide you with all the necessary information you need to know about this important court system. Introduction

The Franklin County Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction that serves the citizens of Franklin County, Virginia. The court has been in existence since the early 1800s and has a long and storied history of providing justice to the people of the county. In this guide, we will explore the history of the court, its jurisdiction, the types of cases it handles, and the services it offers.

History of the Franklin County Circuit Court

The Franklin County Circuit Court was established in 1806, just a few years after Franklin County was formed. The court has undergone several changes over the years, but it has remained a vital part of the county's justice system. The current courthouse was built in 1909 and has undergone several renovations and updates to keep up with the changing times.

Jurisdiction of the Franklin County Circuit Court

The Franklin County Circuit Court has general jurisdiction over all types of cases that arise within the county. This includes both civil and criminal cases, as well as family law, juvenile, and probate cases. The court also has appellate jurisdiction over cases that are appealed from the General District Court and the Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court.

Judges of the Franklin County Circuit Court

The Franklin County Circuit Court currently has three judges who preside over cases. These judges are elected by the Virginia General Assembly and serve eight-year terms. The current judges are Judge William N. Alexander II, Judge Clyde H. Perdue Jr., and Judge Marcie L. Lowe.

Types of Cases Handled by the Franklin County Circuit Court

The Franklin County Circuit Court handles a wide variety of cases, including criminal, civil, family law, juvenile, and probate cases.

Criminal Cases

The Franklin County Circuit Court handles all types of criminal cases, including felonies and misdemeanors. This includes cases such as assault, drug offenses, theft, and DUIs. The court also oversees grand jury proceedings and the trial of serious criminal offenses.

Civil Cases

The Franklin County Circuit Court also has jurisdiction over civil cases, which involve disputes between individuals or entities. This includes cases such as contract disputes, personal injury claims, and property disputes. The court has the authority to hear cases involving any amount of money or damages.

Family Law Cases

The Franklin County Circuit Court handles all types of family law cases, including divorces, child custody disputes, and child support cases. The court also oversees adoptions and name changes.

Juvenile Cases

The Franklin County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over juvenile cases, which involve individuals under the age of 18. This includes cases such as delinquency proceedings, child abuse and neglect cases, and truancy cases.

Probate Cases

The Franklin County Circuit Court handles probate cases, which involve the administration of estates and the distribution of assets after a person's death. This includes cases such as wills, trusts, and guardianships.

Court Services

The Franklin County Circuit Court offers a wide range of services to the public, including notary services, passport applications, and marriage licenses. The court also provides assistance to self-represented litigants, including forms and guidance on court procedures.

Franklin County Circuit Court Rules

The Franklin County Circuit Court operates under a set of rules that govern court procedures and practices. These rules are designed to ensure fairness and consistency in court proceedings and to protect the rights of all parties involved.

FAQs

How do I file a case in the Franklin County Circuit Court?

Filing a case in the Franklin County Circuit Court:

To file a case in the Franklin County Circuit Court, follow these steps:

  1. Determine the type of case you want to file (e.g. civil, criminal, family law, etc.).
  2. Obtain the necessary forms for your specific case type, which can often be found on the court's website or at the court clerk's office.
  3. Fill out the forms accurately and completely, making sure to include any required documentation or fees.
  4. File the completed forms with the court clerk's office in person or by mail, along with any necessary filing fees. The clerk will stamp the forms with the date and time, as well as assign a case number.
  5. Serve a copy of the filed documents on the opposing party or parties, following the appropriate service rules for your jurisdiction.
  6. Monitor your case for updates, attend any scheduled hearings, and follow court instructions.

What is the process for obtaining a marriage license at the Franklin County Circuit Court?

  1. Obtaining a marriage license at the Franklin County Circuit Court:

To obtain a marriage license in Franklin County, follow these steps:

  • Both parties must appear in person at the Franklin County Circuit Court Clerk's office.
  • Bring valid photo identification (e.g. driver's license, passport, or state-issued ID) and proof of age (e.g. birth certificate).
  • Complete the marriage license application and pay the required fee (check with the court for the current fee).
  • If either party has been previously married, bring proof of divorce, annulment, or death of the previous spouse.
  • Wait for any applicable waiting period, if required by local law, before the marriage ceremony can be performed.
  • After the ceremony, the officiant will return the completed marriage license to the court for recording.
